AfterPlayerTurnStart.maps_to: on_player_turn_started (mr_struggles.py:22-31) -- the sim's post-draw turn-start slot, serving both C#'s AfterPlayerTurnStart (audits/seam/turn_structure.json step 22) and AfterSideTurnStart (step 23); executed order via `py tools/audit/relic_probes.py turn-order`
AfterPlayerTurnStart.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The slot, the scaling amount, the props, the dealer and the target set all match (N1-N3), but the port omits the win check its identically shaped sibling relic/mercury_hourglass performs (G1), and shares the two-pass turn-start collapse (G2).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): mr_struggles.py omits the `self._check_win()` that relic/mercury_hourglass -- the same hook, the same AoE shape -- performs, so a lethal turn-start tick leaves the sim in Phase.PLAYER_TURN with every enemy dead
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# runs `await CheckWinCondition()` immediately after the player's turn setup and the auto-pre-play phase (CombatManager.cs:573), so a turn-start tick that kills the last enemy ends the fight there. The sim has NO such check on two paths: turn-1 construction (combat.py:208-209 is on_combat_start then start_turn, followed by nothing) and the EXTRA-TURN path (combat.py:648-652 is `turn += 1; player.start_turn(); return`). Two ported relics compensate by hand-rolling Relic._check_win() -- relics/mercury_hourglass.py:29 and relics/festive_popper.py -- and mr_struggles.py:26-31 does not, so the two ports of the same hook behave differently. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py tools/audit/relic_probes_b09.py b09-struggles): on the extra-turn path with the last enemy at 2 HP, mercury_hourglass ends the combat (phase=COMBAT_OVER, result=player_won=True, turns_taken=2) and mr_struggles does NOT (phase=PLAYER_TURN, result=None) even though all_enemies_dead() is True -- the agent is handed a turn against a dead board, draws a hand, and the fight only ends at the next end_turn, so the recorded turn count and every per-turn counter diverge. Both sides ported and obtainable: Mr Struggles is granted by the ported Doll Room event (events/doll_room.py:15) and the extra turn by relic/paels_eye (Ancient, the ported Pael shrine, relics/paels_eye.py:36-40). SCOPE, stated honestly: a CONTROL row in the same probe shows the ORDINARY end_turn path is covered for both relics by combat.py:681-685, and the turn-1 window needs an enemy already below the tick (the lowest ported enemy max HP is 6, EyeWithTeeth), so the extra-turn window is the reachable one. This is the site-specific observable of audits/seam/turn_structure.json guard G13, which labels the mechanism LIVE and names `mr_struggles.py:22` in its own issue text; one verdict per mechanism, binding rule 3 -- the seam owns the missing CheckWinCondition and this record owns the sibling-inconsistency observable. Rule 7: leans on combat.py, relics/base.py, mercury_hourglass.py, paels_eye.py and the seam record, none hashed here.

guards.what: G2: the sim collapses C#'s two ordered turn-start passes (AfterPlayerTurnStart, step 22; AfterSideTurnStart, step 23) into one flat on_player_turn_started pass in relic order
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# runs turn-start relics in TWO complete, ordered passes -- every `Hook.AfterPlayerTurnStart` listener (audits/seam/turn_structure.json step 22, CombatManager.cs:673-675) finishes before any `Hook.AfterSideTurnStart` listener (step 23, CombatManager.cs:520-524) begins. The sim has ONE flat pass, `on_player_turn_started` (hooks.py:285-295), dispatched in RunState.relics order, so a step-22 relic can run after a step-23 relic. EXECUTED CENSUS (py tools/audit/relic_probes_b09.py b09-simple): 9 ported relics whose C# hook is AfterPlayerTurnStart land on the sim's on_player_turn_started (bellows, choices_paradox, festive_popper, gambling_chip, mercury_hourglass, mr_struggles, pendulum, royal_poison, vexing_puzzlebox) and 14 whose C# hook is AfterSideTurnStart land on the SAME method (akabeko, bone_tea, bread, brimstone, candelabra, chandelier, crossbow, fake_happy_flower, happy_flower, lantern, paels_tears, sai, seal_of_gold, very_hot_cocoa). THE MECHANISM IS LIVE, proved by execution on a step-22 x step-23 pair: Gambling Chip (GamblingChip.cs:16, step 22) mulligans the opening hand and Bone Tea (step 23) upgrades it, so C# always upgrades the POST-mulligan hand. The sim gives hand upgrade levels [1,1,1,1,1] for relic order [gambling_chip, bone_tea] and [0,0,0,0,1] for [bone_tea, gambling_chip] -- and Bone Tea's single charge is spent either way. Both relics are ported and obtainable (Gambling Chip is Rare in the grab bag, Bone Tea is bought at the ported Tea Master event), and either acquisition order is possible. This relic's OWN observable at this site is not separately demonstrated: the site inherits the mechanism's verdict per binding rule 3. Related but NOT identical to audits/seam/turn_structure.json guard G12, which flattens the Late/VeryEarly SUB-phases of one hook; this is two DIFFERENT C# hooks collapsed, with a wider blast radius (9 x 14 relic pairs). Reported as a pool-wide shape in .superpowers/sdd/relic-batch-09-lessons.md. Rule 7: leans on hooks.py, GamblingChip.cs and BoneTea.cs, none hashed here.

guards.what: N1: the damage amount is `base.Owner.PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber` (MrStruggles.cs:21) vs `self.turn` == CombatState.turn (mr_struggles.py:28)
guards.rationale: The two counters agree, including on the case that could have broken them. PlayerCombatState.TurnNumber starts at 1 (PlayerCombatState.cs:37) and is incremented by IncrementTurnNumber (cs:157-159) from CombatManager's side switch (CombatManager.cs:1405-1418); crucially that code increments TurnNumber for an EXTRA player turn while leaving `_state.RoundNumber` alone, and the source's own doc comment (PlayerCombatState.cs:33-36) names Pael's Eye as the reason. The sim's CombatState.turn also starts at 1 (combat.py:108) and increments on BOTH the ordinary boundary (combat.py:674) and the extra-turn path (combat.py:650), so it tracks TurnNumber and not RoundNumber -- the right one for this relic. The sim has a single counter serving both C# concepts; nothing in this relic reads RoundNumber, so the conflation is not observable here. Rule 7: leans on combat.py and the two C# files, none hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `ValueProp.Unpowered` passed directly (MrStruggles.cs:21) with dealer = base.Owner.Creature and no cardSource
guards.rationale: DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (valueprops.py:42) is `ValueProp.UNPOWERED` alone, matching exactly: the damage is NOT boosted by Strength (is_powered_attack requires MOVE, valueprops.py:47-49), IS blockable (no Unblockable flag), and is not a 'hit' for on_attacked/Curl Up (cmds.py:69 gates that on MOVE). Note this relic has NO CanonicalVars/DamageVar at all -- the amount is the live turn number, so there is no constant to check and no AscensionHelper branch anywhere in the file. The port passes `dealer=self.combat.player`, which is the same creature as the hook's `player` argument that relic/mercury_hourglass passes.

The owner check is single-player-structural -- on_player_turn_started only fires for the player. On the enemy set: C# passes `combatState.HittableEnemies` == `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142), and IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(CombatState, this)` (Creature.cs:285-299). The sim passes Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:294-297), which filters only `not e.is_gone` (dead or escaped) -- but the missing predicate IS applied, one target later, by DamageCmd.deal itself: `if not hooks.should_allow_hitting(target): return 0` (cmds.py:51-52). So for a DAMAGE call site the two sets are observationally identical (an alive-but-unhittable enemy is iterated and then takes 0). DELIBERATELY DISTINGUISHED from relic/bag_of_marbles guard G2, which records the same call-site substitution as a gap: that site routes through PowerCmd.apply, which has NO such backstop (audits/seam/power_cmd.json gap G6, the missing CanReceivePowers check). Same substitution, different downstream, so different verdicts -- and binding rule 3 is satisfied because the MECHANISM under verdict there is the missing PowerCmd backstop, not living_enemies() itself. The `escaped` half is also covered: an escaped creature is IsDead-or-removed in C# and is_gone in the sim.
